items.title: Bug: user creation accepts empty payloads and client-controlled ids
items.body:
## Description

The `/api/users` creation path accepts arbitrary request bodies and forwards them directly to `createUser`. The service currently builds the user object as `{ id: `usr_${Date.now()}`, ...payload }`, so a caller can submit an `id` field and override the generated server ID. Empty or malformed payloads are also accepted because the controller does not validate `req.body`.

## Impact

- Clients can create users with attacker-chosen IDs.
- Empty objects can become persisted-looking user records once storage is added.
- Downstream admin and profile views can receive malformed user records without `name`, `email`, or a safe role.

## Expected behavior

Validate user creation input, reject unknown fields such as `id`, require a valid name and email, allow only public user roles, and keep the server-generated user ID authoritative.

## Files

- `apps/api/src/controllers/userController.js`
- `apps/api/src/services/userService.js`

items.title: Job budget validation does not reject inverted range where min exceeds max
items.body:
Parent Algora bounty: #743

`createJobSchema` in `validators/job.js` validates `budgetMin` and `budgetMax` individually as non-negative numbers but does not enforce `budgetMax >= budgetMin`. A payload with `{ budgetMin: 500, budgetMax: 100 }` passes schema validation and is stored as a semantically invalid job listing.

## Scope
Modify `apps/api/src/validators/job.js` only. Do not touch the job controller, service, or routes.

3. Run npm test.

The health test (and future src/tests/*.test.js files) should run.

## Proposed fix

Change the workspace script to an explicit test glob, for example node --test src/tests/*.test.js, or use the supported Node test-directory invocation for the project's minimum Node version. Add a regression check so npm test is exercised from the repository root.

items.title: [SECURITY] Client-Controlled IDs via Object Spread in Services (user, notification, message)
items.body:
## Bug: Client-Controlled IDs via Object Spread in Services

### Severity: HIGH

### Locations
- `apps/api/src/services/userService.js` line 8: `{ id: ..., ...payload }`
- `apps/api/src/services/notificationService.js` line 8: `{ id: ..., read: false, ...payload }`
- `apps/api/src/services/messageService.js` line 8: `{ id: ..., ...payload }`

### Description
These services use object spread (`...payload`) after setting server-controlled fields like `id` and `read`. A malicious client can include `id` or `read` in the request body, which will override the server-generated values due to JavaScript's object spread semantics. For notifications, clients can set `read: true` to mark notifications as read without authorization.

### Impact
- Client-controlled resource IDs (potential ID collision / enumeration)
- Notification read status manipulation
- Message ID injection

### Fix
Explicitly assign server-controlled fields AFTER the spread:
```js
const user = { ...payload, id: `usr_${Date.now()}` };
```
Or use destructuring to strip client-controlled fields.

items.title: [BUG] Register Token Subject May Not Match Returned User ID (Date.now() Race)
items.body:
## Bug: Register Token Subject Does Not Match Returned User ID

### Severity: MEDIUM

### Location
`apps/api/src/services/authService.js`:
```js
export async function registerUser(payload) {
  return {
    id: `usr_${Date.now()}`,        // First call to Date.now()
    email: payload.email,
    role: payload.role,
    token: signAccessToken({ sub: `usr_${Date.now()}`, role: payload.role })  // Second call
  };
}
```

### Description
The `registerUser` function calls `Date.now()` TWICE — once for the returned `id` and once for the token's `sub` claim. Between these two calls, `Date.now()` can return different values (different millisecond), causing a mismatch between the user ID and the token subject. The JWT will reference a user ID that doesn't match the returned user.

Note: Due to JavaScript's synchronous execution and typical millisecond resolution, this may not always manifest, but it is a race condition that CAN occur.

### Impact
- Token subject mismatch (token references wrong user ID)
- Authentication/inconsistency issues

### Fix
Generate the ID once and reuse it:
```js
const id = `usr_${Date.now()}`;
return { id, email: payload.email, role: payload.role, token: signAccessToken({ sub: id, role: payload.role }) };
```

---

items.body:
## Bugs (5)

### 1. CORS allows any origin
app.js uses cors() with no origin restriction. Any website can make authenticated cross-origin requests to this API.

### 2. No request body size limit
express.json() is called without a limit option. Attackers can send arbitrarily large JSON payloads causing memory exhaustion.

### 3. jobService mass assignment
createJob spreads raw payload after defaults: { id, status, ...payload }. A caller can override id, status, or inject arbitrary fields.

### 4. messageService sender impersonation
sendMessage spreads raw payload allowing callers to set any senderId, impersonating other users.

### 5. Job validator allows budgetMin > budgetMax
createJobSchema validates both as nonnegative but does not enforce budgetMin <= budgetMax.

## Expected fixes

1. Restrict CORS to configurable allowed origins (env.CORS_ORIGINS)
2. Add express.json({ limit: '1mb' })
3. Only use validated fields from schema parse, do not spread raw body
4. Bind message sender from req.user, ignore payload senderId
5. Add .refine() to ensure budgetMin <= budgetMax

## Scope

- apps/api/src/app.js
- apps/api/src/config/env.js
